messages:
Evelyn: Heads-up: I want to canonicalize the BatchDescriptor lifecycle. Right now different teams bake payloads differently and we get nondeterministic replays. Proposal: immutable descriptors + tombstones + rehydrate API. Thoughts?

Ajay: Sounds useful. What do you mean by tombstones here?

Evelyn: Tombstone = descriptor marked retired/invalid with reason + rev. We keep it for audit and to avoid accidental reruns. Rehydrate API maps descriptor id -> exact payload snapshot (or error if tombstoned).

Leah: We need fingerprint/version fields. If descriptor points to mutable objectstore path, fingerprint lets orchestrator validate it matches what sampler intended.

Tom: Agree on immutability. Also consider descriptor pinning: descriptors should include model-compat hints (runtime profile id) so orchestrator can pick a compatible kernel path.

Ravi: Operationally, if a descriptor is tombstoned because payload corrupted, do we auto-generate replacement descriptors or require manual sampler review?

Evelyn: I prefer manual for now to avoid masking upstream issues. But we can surface suggestions: "closest snapshot" or "quantized fallback descriptor" for operator convenience.

Ajay: For private deployments we must ensure descriptor metadata never leaks. Descriptor should have a storage_class field: public|private. If private, rehydrate API returns a signed URL valid only within VPC or returns an error if invoked outside tenant scope.

Leah: Observability: emit descriptor lineage (origin sampler id, policy, rollout tag) and rehydrate events. Console can show when a descriptor was tombstoned and why.

Tom: One more: canonical store should support lightweight diffs so sampler can publish "delta" descriptors when policy tweak only changes sample weight, not payload. This helps audits.

benchbot: noted: descriptor-canonicalization proposed. fingerprint-required=true; tombstone-policy=manual-only; private_storage_scoped=true.

Evelyn: Next steps: I'll add descriptor lifecycle section to RFC and a small PoC for tombstone+rehydrate APIs. Leah — want to help define fingerprint scheme?

Leah: Yep, I'll draft fingerprint spec (sha256 of normalized payload + metadata canonicalization).
